title: A promoted library logo could hold bytes its verified ledger row does not name
body:
## Summary
promoteLogos deduped the shared logo library by sha256 but stored files under the per-entity name, and promoted session-writable files without re-hashing them.

## Description
apps/server/src/generation/finalize.ts promoteLogos (before 0b7feeb) skipped rows whose sha256 was already in data/assets/logos/LEDGER.json, then copyFileSync(src, lib/<basename>) - assets.ts names files per entity (ferrari.png), so a second, different Ferrari mark from a later job overwrote the first file while both rows (licence, author, sha256) stayed. It also copied whatever sat in work/assets/ (writable by the session's Write tool) under the server-written commons-api row. refs.ts staged library logos by basename(r.file), so it could not see a renamed copy either. Registry: concurrency-guards/idempotency-by-design (identity survives reuse: the hash is the identity, the name is not). Fixed: promote only when sha256(file) == row.sha256 (finalize.ts:111); a different file under a taken name gets a -<sha8> suffix (finalize.ts:116); refs.ts:121 stages library_file.

## Flow
- job 1 fetches Commons ferrari.png (A) and finalizes: lib/ferrari.png = A, row A
- job 2 fetches a different ferrari.png (B): sha B not in the ledger -> copy over lib/ferrari.png
- row A now describes bytes B: a later session reusing row A credits A's licence/author for image B
- or: the session rewrites work/assets/logos/x.png after fetch_asset -> promoted under the verified row

## Expected impact
Every library logo keeps the licence and author that belong to its bytes (the owner's attribution trail). Could break: nothing reads the old overwrite behaviour; older rows without library_file fall back to file.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every library row's file has the row's sha256
Before: two same-name logos -> 2 rows, 1 distinct library_file, row 1's sha != its file; a rewritten work/ file promoted (2 tests red on HEAD's finalize.ts); refs staged 1 of 2
After: 2 rows, 2 files, each file matches its sha; tampered file not promoted; refs stages both (29/29 finalize.test.ts + refs.test.ts)
Method: gate - finalize.test.ts 'logo library promotion' + refs.test.ts library_file case, seeded red on HEAD
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
apps/server/src/generation/finalize.ts:105-120 (HEAD~ before: `copyFileSync(src, path.join(lib, path.basename(src)))`, no hash check)
apps/server/src/generation/assets.ts:296 `let name = `${slug(input.entity)}.${ext}`` (per-entity names)
apps/server/src/generation/refs.ts:121 (was `path.basename(r.file)`)

title: The worker found its render job by scanning the newest 50 jobs of every kind
body:
## Summary
callbacks.renderStatus searched GET /api/jobs (runner.list(undefined, 50)) for the render id, so a render with 50 newer jobs behind it was 'not found' and its generation job failed.

## Description
apps/server/src/generation/callbacks.ts renderStatus (before 53ced4a) fetched /api/jobs - apps/server/src/app.ts:331 `runner.list(undefined, 50)`, the newest 50 jobs of every kind - and threw `render job ... not found` when the id was not in that page. During a long video render the owner can enqueue ingest/transform/render/audio jobs; past 50 the poll threw, waitForRender rethrew, and the paid generation job failed as error_kind render although its render succeeded. Registry: bounded-enumeration/filter-after-return-under-limit (a page used as a lookup). Fixed: GET /api/generation/renders/:renderId (routes.ts:200, gen_render rows only, 404 otherwise); renderStatus calls it (callbacks.ts:32).

## Flow
- worker requests a gen_render (video, minutes)
- owner or a pipeline enqueues 50+ other jobs
- the 1 s poll lists /api/jobs: the render is not on the page
- renderStatus throws -> job failed (render), spend lost

## Expected impact
Generation jobs survive a busy job runner; each poll reads one row instead of 50. Could break: a client still using /api/jobs for this (none: worker-process.test's stand-in was updated).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - render status resolves by id
Before: render succeeded, 60 jobs enqueued after it -> renderStatus rejects 'not found' (red on HEAD)
After: resolves {status: succeeded}; unknown id -> 404 (162/162 generation/)
Method: gate - routes.test.ts drives httpCallbacks against the real route set incl. app.ts's /api/jobs page
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/app.ts:331 `app.get("/api/jobs", (c) => c.json({ jobs: d.runner.list(undefined, 50) }))`
apps/server/src/generation/callbacks.ts (before) `const j = r.jobs.find((x) => x.id === id); if (!j) throw new Error(`render job ${id} not found`)`

title: Generation runner decoded the CLI stream per chunk; only the co-pilot was fixed
body:
## Summary
generation/claude.ts did buf += d.toString('utf8') per stdout/stderr chunk; 762d7fb fixed the same rule only in the co-pilot's ClaudeEngine.

## Description
One rule, two runners. packages/llm ClaudeEngine got setEncoding('utf8') in 762d7fb; apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts kept per-chunk decoding, so a multibyte character cut at a pipe boundary became two U+FFFD in run.jsonl (audit stream), run.log, the relayed progress note and the job error - and this runner logs driver/team names. Registry: streaming-output/stream-parsing ('carry the tail'). Fixed: setEncoding on both pipes (claude.ts:171-173). New instrument claude-stream.test.ts mocks spawn with a fake child (no CLI, nothing paid).

## Flow
- CLI emits a result/text line with 'Raikkonen' (a-umlaut)
- the pipe cuts between the two UTF-8 bytes
- each chunk decoded alone -> U+FFFD U+FFFD in run.jsonl and run.log

## Expected impact
Names in generation logs and errors stay intact. Could break: nothing; data handlers now receive strings.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stream text survives chunk boundaries
Before: split a-umlaut -> run.jsonl lacks 'Kimi Raikkonen leads' (red on HEAD)
After: run.jsonl, run.log, stderr.log intact, no U+FFFD (14/14)
Method: gate - claude-stream.test.ts fake child fed byte chunks
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts:162-163 (before) `child.stdout.on("data", (d: Buffer) => { buf += d.toString("utf8");`
git show 762d7fb -- packages/llm/src/index.ts (the co-pilot fix)

title: An unwritable run.jsonl crashed the generation worker mid-run
body:
## Summary
The run.jsonl append in the stdout handler was unguarded while run.log and stderr.log appends are best effort; a throw escaped as an uncaught exception.

## Description
apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts onLine (before dd26d31) called appendFileSync(p.runJsonl) bare inside the stream 'data' handler; worker.ts logLine and the stderr.log append are try/catch. On Windows an AV scanner or indexer holding the file (EBUSY/EPERM) or a full disk killed the worker process: the row stayed running, the queue stalled until a manual restart, and the spawned CLI kept running and spending. Fixed: try/catch, one run.log line naming run.jsonl (claude.ts:143-151).

## Flow
- a live run streams events
- run.jsonl append throws (locked / disk full)
- exception escapes the 'data' handler -> worker process exits
- CLI child orphaned; job 'running' until recover()

## Expected impact
The worker survives a log-file hiccup and the run completes. Could break: run.jsonl may miss lines (said once in run.log).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a log write failure does not kill the worker
Before: run.jsonl unwritable -> EISDIR escapes uncaught, run never settles (red)
After: run resolves with cost/turns, no uncaught exception, one run.log line (15/15)
Method: gate - claude-stream.test.ts with run.jsonl made a directory
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts:142 (before) `appendFileSync(p.runJsonl, `${line}\n`);` (no try)
apps/server/src/generation/worker.ts:231-233 logLine `try { appendFileSync(...) } catch { /* log is best effort */ }`

title: compute_timing_plan accepted plans no props file can match (40/600/30)
body:
## Summary
TimingInput allowed 1-40 entities, 600 periods and 30 events while props (which must match the plan exactly) are capped at 2-10, 120 and 12.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:132,158 require props periods/entities to equal the plan's; DATA_RACE_LIMITS (packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:55-61) caps props at maxEntities 10, maxPeriods 120, maxEvents 12. apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts TimingInput (before 3959f42) accepted 1-40/600/30, so a session could build its props around a plan the validator must reject. Fixed: bounds from DATA_RACE_LIMITS (mcp-tools.ts:32-37).

## Flow
- session computes a plan over 15 entities or 200 periods: ok + sha
- writes props around it
- validate_generation_output rejects; session recomputes (paid turns)

## Expected impact
Out-of-range plans are refused at the tool with the field named. Could break: no caller passes more (e2e runs fake mode).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the plan tool enforces the props' limits
Before: 4 of 4 out-of-limit inputs (11 entities, 1 entity, 121 periods, 13 events) returned ok: true (probe on HEAD)
After: 4 of 4 refused naming the field; 12 events still ok (165/165)
Method: gate - mcp-tools.test.ts new case, red on HEAD
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts (before) `periods: z.array(...).min(2).max(600), entities: ...min(1).max(40), events ...max(30)`
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:56,60,61 maxEntities 10, maxPeriods 120, maxEvents 12

title: compute_timing_plan publishes z.any() while the handler enforces TimingInput
body:
## Summary
The generation catalog advertised 5 untyped compute_timing_plan args and a hand-copied fetch_asset shape; the handlers validate with TimingInput / FetchAssetInput.

## Description
Lane B card from the LLM Co-pilot round, owned and built here. apps/server/src/mcp.ts registered compute_timing_plan with periods/entities/values/events/opts all z.any().optional() and fetch_asset with its own copy of the shape (no length limits, its own kind list). Registry mcp-tools/tool-schema-design: the published and enforced schema are one artifact. Fixed: TimingInput exported; mcp.ts:66,69 register FetchAssetInput.shape and {job_id, ...TimingInput.shape}; SDK-side rejections come back as isError results naming the field. Coupled: apps/server/src/mcp.ts, mcp-scope.test.ts (LLM Co-pilot context; handed over by the director).

## Flow
- generation agent lists tools: compute_timing_plan args untyped
- calls with a guessed shape
- TimingInput rejects; agent iterates on error text

## Expected impact
The agent sees types and limits before calling; fewer failed calls. Could break: a call the SDK now rejects before the handler (same rules).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the advertised schema equals the enforced one
Before: 5 of 5 compute_timing_plan args published as {} (only job_id required); fetch_asset url/entity unbounded (red on HEAD)
After: periods/entities/values required and typed with DATA_RACE_LIMITS bounds, opts additionalProperties false, fetch_asset kind enum = ASSET_KINDS, url <= 2000; 11-entity call isError, valid call reaches handler (170/170)
Method: gate - mcp-scope.test.ts listTools + callTool over InMemoryTransport
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/mcp.ts:67 (before) `periods: z.any().optional(), entities: z.any().optional(), values: z.any().optional(), events: z.any().optional(), opts: z.any().optional()`
apps/server/src/generation/assets.ts:20 `export const FetchAssetInput = z.object({...})`

title: Generation prompts teach WebSearch/WebFetch even when config turns them off
body:
## Summary
visual-options.md and generate-video.md named WebSearch and WebFetch unconditionally; buildClaudeArgs grants them only when config.web.search/fetch are on.

## Description
Lane B card from the LLM Co-pilot round, owned and built here. packages/llm/prompts/generation/visual-options.md:23 and generate-video.md:20 named both tools; apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts:50-55 adds them only per config. Registry prompt-assembly/capability-documentation (never teach a tool the dispatcher denies). Fixed: {{WEB_FIND}} rendered by webFindText(config.web) (prompt.ts:24); renderPrompt REQUIRES the web flags so the caller cannot forget them; stage passes o.config.web. Coupled: the two templates (no replay fixture keys on them).

## Flow
- owner sets web.search=false, web.fetch=false
- agent follows the prompt and calls WebSearch
- denied; paid turns wasted before the wordmark fallback

## Expected impact
With web off the prompt says so and names fetch_asset only. Default config text unchanged in meaning.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the prompt names only tools the run has
Before: 2 of 2 templates name WebSearch and WebFetch whatever the config (test red on HEAD signature)
After: web off -> 0 of 2 name either tool and both say web is off; search-only/fetch-only name only that tool (14/14 claude-args.test.ts)
Method: gate - claude-args.test.ts renders all four config combinations and checks buildClaudeArgs agrees
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/llm/prompts/generation/visual-options.md:23 (before) 'Use WebSearch and WebFetch to find the Commons file page'
apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts:50-51 `if (config.web.search) tools.push("WebSearch"); if (config.web.fetch) tools.push("WebFetch");`

title: Incremental run log split a UTF-8 character (and lines) at its 1 MB read cap
body:
## Summary
GET /api/generation/jobs/:id/log decoded up to 1 MB from offset with toString; a cut multibyte character became U+FFFD on both sides of the seam.

## Description
apps/server/src/generation/routes.ts log route (before 59a8ef3) returned buf.toString('utf8') for up to 1,000,000 bytes and next = start + buf.length; the LogDrawer (apps/studio/src/board/LogDrawer.tsx) appends chunks and continues at next. The 'partial' state of a growing file (cap or a line mid-append) was unhandled. Fixed: end on the last newline (routes.ts:113); a newline-free read is held unless it is a full 1 MB read.

## Flow
- a long session's run.log passes 1 MB
- the drawer's read cap lands inside an a-umlaut
- chunk 1 ends with U+FFFD, chunk 2 starts with one

## Expected impact
The owner's log view never shows mangled names at a seam. Could break: a final line without a newline is not shown (logLine always writes one).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - log chunks are whole lines
Before: 999,999 ASCII bytes + lines starting with a-umlaut -> chunk ends in U+FFFD, not on a newline (red on HEAD)
After: no U+FFFD, every chunk ends in a newline, chunks concatenate to the file; partial trailing line -> '' with next unchanged (11/11)
Method: gate - routes.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/server/src/generation/routes.ts:93-96 (at 78400b9) `const buf = Buffer.alloc(Math.min(size - start, 1_000_000)); ... body = buf.toString("utf8"); next = start + buf.length;`

title: A configured timeout above ~24.8 days failed every job after 1 ms
body:
## Summary
armTimeout passed timeoutMin * 60_000 to setTimeout; Node clamps delays above 2^31-1 ms to 1 ms.

## Description
apps/server/src/generation/worker.ts armTimeout (before ab21788); GenerationConfigSchema bounds timeoutMin only as positive (packages/schemas/src/generation.ts:127). A large value meant as 'effectively unlimited' aborted every job at once with 'no result within N min (configured timeout)'. Fixed: clamp to 2^31-1 ms (worker.ts:47,54).

## Flow
- owner sets timeoutMin 1000000
- job starts; setTimeout(6e10) -> TimeoutOverflowWarning, fires at 1 ms
- job failed as timeout, message blames the limit

## Expected impact
Large timeouts behave as long timeouts. Could break: nothing (24.8 days > any run).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the timer honours the configured limit
Before: timeoutMin 1,000,000 -> onTimeout fired within 30 ms (red on HEAD)
After: not fired, no warning (33/33 queue.test.ts)
Method: gate - queue.test.ts real timer
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Live sessions got a stale 'lands with T9' note instead of the props schema
body:
## Summary
The live engine never passed propsJsonSchema to stageRefs, so every MANIFEST.json and params_json.refs.pending carried a stale 'pending' note.

## Description
apps/server/src/generation/refs.ts:108-112 writes refs/data-race-props.schema.json only when given propsJsonSchema, else pushes 'data-race-props.schema.json (DataRaceProps lands with T9; ...)' into pending. apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts stage called stageRefs without it although dataRacePropsJsonSchema exists (mcp-tools.ts serves it). Fixed: claude.ts:115 passes it; refs.ts option doc updated.

## Flow
- live job prepares
- refs/MANIFEST.json pending: schema 'lands with T9'
- session reads a stale claim; schema file absent from refs/

## Expected impact
The session finds the schema beside the other references; nothing pending. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - staged references state what exists
Before: stageRefs called without propsJsonSchema; refs.pending has 1 entry (red on HEAD)
After: schema staged, refs.pending [] (17/17)
Method: gate - claude-stream.test.ts mocks ./refs and checks the options
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts:114 (before) `stageRefs({ paths: p, repoRoot, dataRoot: o.dataRoot })`
apps/server/src/generation/refs.ts:113 `pending.push("data-race-props.schema.json (DataRaceProps lands with T9; ...)")`

title: Job detail read the whole run.log every 2 s poll to return 200 lines
body:
## Summary
The detail route's log_tail did readFileSync(run.log) + split for each LogDrawer poll.

## Description
apps/server/src/generation/routes.ts tail() (before c3f3ec0) read the full file; apps/studio/src/board/LogDrawer.tsx:23 polls the detail every 2 s while a job runs. Fixed: read the last 512 KB (routes.ts:44), drop the cut line, take the last 200.

## Flow
- LogDrawer open on a running job
- every 2 s: GET detail -> whole-file sync read on the event loop

## Expected impact
Less event-loop time per poll on long logs. Could break: nothing; same 200 lines (test).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - detail request time on a long log
Before: 16.9 ms per detail request (5 MB run.log, 20 requests, real route)
After: 5.7 ms per request, identical log_tail (12/12 routes.test.ts)
Method: probe - timed the real route on HEAD and on the change with the same 5 MB file; the gate pins equal output
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Rejecting a case missed active jobs older than the newest 500 job rows
body:
## Summary
GenerationFlow.cancelActive filtered the newest 500 rows of every status in JS; queueGuard filters by status in SQL.

## Description
apps/server/src/generation/flow.ts cancelActive (before 58eb32c) used queue.list({ limit: 500 }); generation_jobs rows are never pruned and retry re-queues an old row with its original created_at, so a retried job behind 500 newer rows survived the reject and still ran. Registry: bounded-enumeration/filter-after-return-under-limit. Fixed: list queued and running by status (flow.ts:34). New instrument flow.test.ts (GenerationFlow had no unit test).

## Flow
- owner retries an old failed job (created_at kept)
- 500+ newer job rows exist
- owner rejects the case -> cancelActive misses the job -> it runs and spends

## Expected impact
A reject always stops that case's queued and running jobs. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - reject cancels every active job of the case
Before: retried job behind 600 newer rows stays queued; running one gets no cancel request (2/2 red on HEAD)
After: cancelled / cancel requested (2/2; app.generation.test.ts 16/16)
Method: gate - generation/flow.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/generation/flow.ts:30 (before) `for (const j of this.d.queue.list({ limit: 500 })) if (ACTIVE.includes(j.status) && filter(j))`
apps/server/src/generation-guard.ts:23 `queue.list({ status, limit: 500 })` (the filtered sibling)

title: The prompt's 'reuse a logo from refs/logos' path can never pass validation
body:
## Summary
generate-video.md tells the session to reuse library logos, but rule 3 needs an out/assets.json row for the logo path and the prompt forbids editing that ledger; nothing else writes one.

## Description
packages/llm/prompts/generation/generate-video.md:20 says reuse a logo from refs/logos/ when LEDGER.json lists it. checkGenerationRules (packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:190-192) requires a row in out/assets.json whose path equals logo.path; resolveLogoPath (apps/server/src/generation/validate-data-race.ts:45-46) accepts only assets/... or data/assets/logos/... (not refs/logos/...); prepare.ts:52 seeds out/assets.json with []; only fetch_asset appends; visual-options.md:23 says 'never edit it'. So the documented reuse either fails rule 3 or requires the session to disobey the prompt. Candidate fix: prepare seeds out/assets.json with the library rows under path data/assets/logos/<library_file> and the prompt names that path (or a reuse_logo tool). Registry prompt-assembly/capability-documentation.

## Flow
- a later job finds Ferrari in refs/logos/LEDGER.json
- props use logo.path refs/logos/ferrari.png -> logo-file-missing; or data/assets/logos/ferrari.png -> logo-no-ledger-row
- session must refetch (paid turns, Wikimedia load) or edit the ledger it was told not to touch

## Expected impact
Library reuse works as documented: fewer fetches and turns. Could break: the validator's ledger semantics (rows the session did not fetch).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the documented reuse path validates
Before: 0 of 2 reuse spellings validate (walked: refs/... -> logo-file-missing, data/assets/logos/... -> logo-no-ledger-row)
After: predicted: seeded rows make data/assets/logos/<file> validate
Method: simulation - walked the validator and prompt; an M change across prepare.ts, the prompt and possibly the rules, too wide to land unread
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: validate-data-race test: stage a library logo + its LEDGER row, run prepare, write props with the prompt's reuse path, validateDataRaceOutputs -> ok (A: logo-no-ledger-row / logo-file-missing)

title: Finalize trusts the session-writable out/assets.json for logo licence and author
body:
## Summary
Validation and the video manifest read logo provenance from work/out/assets.json, which the session can edit; the server-written fetched-assets.json is used only for library promotion.

## Description
fetch_asset appends each row to out/assets.json AND to <job>/fetched-assets.json, 'the authoritative copy ... where the session cannot write' (apps/server/src/generation/assets.ts:305-307). But validateDataRaceOutputs reads ledger rows from out/assets.json (validate-data-race.ts:120-123) and the video manifest copies them (finalize.ts:178,202), so a session with Write can declare CC0 / any author for a model-declared or Commons file and the manifest records it. Fix: cross-check every used logo's row against fetched-assets.json (sha256, licence, author, verified_by) or read provenance from it; fake-mode fixtures need a fetched-assets.json too (sample-fixtures.ts).

## Flow
- session fetches a CC-BY-SA logo
- edits out/assets.json: licence CC0, author blank-filled
- validation passes; manifest.assets carries the edited licence

## Expected impact
A generated video's licence record always comes from the server's own fetch. Could break: fake-mode fixtures and sample-fixtures test until they carry the authoritative ledger.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - provenance in the manifest is server-verified
Before: manifest licence = whatever out/assets.json says (walked)
After: predicted: an edited row is refused naming the logo
Method: simulation - walked assets.ts/validate-data-race.ts/finalize.ts; M with fixture regeneration, risk 4
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
apps/server/src/generation/assets.ts:305-307 `this.appendLedger(ledgerFile, row); // the authoritative copy lives outside work/, where the session cannot write`
apps/server/src/generation/validate-data-race.ts:120-123 ledger from out/assets.json
apps/server/src/generation/finalize.ts:178,202 manifest assets from out/assets.json
instrument: finalize.test.ts: fetched-assets.json says CC-BY-SA, out/assets.json edited to CC0 -> finalize refuses naming the logo (A: video recorded with CC0)
